steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: : The Earth's early atmosphere was formed by intense volcanic activity . It contained large amounts of carbon dioxide and water vapour , with nitrogen and small amounts of ammonia and methane . There was little or no oxygen . | : The atmosphere changed over billions of years through several key processes: condensation of water vapour , dissolving of CO₂ in oceans , and photosynthesis by plants and algae . | Algae and plants: evolved and carried out photosynthesis . This removed CO₂ from the atmosphere and produced oxygen . Over time, oxygen built up in the atmosphere. | : As oxygen levels increased, some oxygen formed ozone (O₃) in the upper atmosphere. The ozone layer shields the Earth's surface from harmful UV radiation , allowing more complex organisms to evolve and survive on land.
